_comment: Project-scoped settings shipped with the evolve-loop plugin. Four PreToolUse hooks add defence in depth in Claude Code panes only; the CLI-neutral layers that hold each guarantee for every family are the OS sandbox write rules, the worktree fence and the ship gates (ADR-0154 I-7, docs/architecture/llm-isolation.md section 9.1): (1) ship on Bash — a ship-class git/gh command must itself be the native evolve ship CLI, judged per simple command. (2) phase on Agent|Task — outside a phase cell (no EVOLVE_PHASE marker) while a cycle is active, denies an Agent or Task call whose subagent_type names a phase persona (evolve-*), so a session cannot act as a phase; inside a cell every Agent and Task call passes, because a phase agent may start any subagent of its own harness and the cell boundary is the real limit; the marker is advisory, which is acceptable for defence in depth (ADR-0075; phase ORDER is enforced by the go/internal/core state machine, not this hook). (3) role on Edit|Write — files can only be modified by the active phase within its allowlisted paths, judged on the clean path. (4) docdelete on Bash — blocks rm/mv on docs/** or knowledge-base/** without canonical archival mv. Each hook prefers the freshly-built go/bin/evolve and falls back to the tracked go/evolve when go/bin is missing, so the kernel fails closed even if build outputs are wiped. The guards read no environment except the advisory EVOLVE_PHASE cell marker of the phase guard; the emergency bypass is the guard command's --bypass flag, and routine bypassing is a CLAUDE.md violation. PostToolUse on Edit|Write syntax-checks the modified file by extension; it never blocks, only emits WARN to the agent's stderr.
